correctness.rationale: The finite domain has exactly six antipodal pairs of the 12 explicitly specified vertices, hence 2^6=64 configurations. Read the source's exhaustive exact Z[phi] support-plane, facet-cycle, outward determinant certificate; its sign comparisons are exact since phi=(1+sqrt5)/2. Reconstructed the hull independently using a separate scipy.spatial.ConvexHull algorithm for every one of 64 signed selections and compared to the four algebraic levels, obtaining counts 12/20/20/12 with numerical discrepancies below 2e-13. The original exact integer-pair certificate establishes the finite exhaustive claim; floating corroboration is not a separate exact proof. The scale is edge length two and neither degeneracies nor arbitrary antipodal sets are claimed.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks corroborate, but where the statement is infinite only the reconstructed analytic argument justifies the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: An antipodal selection is a canonical combinatorial class for a centrally symmetric regular polyhedron. Its full exact volume distribution, not merely an arbitrary selected configuration, resolves a natural finite extremal-statistic classification with a meaningful maximum/minimum and orbit multiplicities. It is deliberately restricted to the icosahedron and not claimed to settle higher-dimensional antipodal optimization.
residual_risks: Significance is confined to the precise object/invariant and exact scope stated, not a general theory beyond it.

final_claim: Across all 64 one-per-antipodal-pair six-vertex convex hulls in the edge-2 regular icosahedron, the exact volumes are (4+2phi)/3, (4+6phi)/3, (4+8phi)/3 and (6+8phi)/3, with multiplicities 12,20,20,12 respectively.
